office: Tennessee Secretary of State, Division of Elections

headers_needed.User-Agent: a desktop browser User-Agent string (the relay User-Agent gets 403 from CloudFront)

feeds.notes: https://www.elections.tn.gov/ redirects here. Each contest is a <div class="chart-container" data-race="Governor" id="chart-Governor" data-candidates="[…]"> whose data-candidates attribute is HTML-entity-encoded JSON: [{"name":"Marsha Blackburn","party":"Republican","votes":957136}, …]. Unescape the attribute, then JSON.parse. The human title is the following <h3 class="chart-title">, the status is in .unofficial-indicator-text ('Final Unofficial Results') and the progress in .county-reporting-header-text ('95 of 95 Counties Completed'). Cache-Control: no-store.

feeds.what: US Senate and 9 US House districts (10 contests)
Tennessee Senate (odd districts) and Tennessee House of Representatives (116 contests)
live updates as Server-Sent Events (what the page listens to on election night)
feeds.notes: Answered 200, Content-Type text/event-stream, Content-Length 0: now that results are 'Final Unofficial' the stream is empty, so I could not capture an event. From /js/barchartd3.js (saved as js-barchartd3.js): streams are /server-sent-events/<categoryGroup> (governor, congressional, general-assembly, constitutional-amendments), /server-sent-events/following, /server-sent-events/results-by-county/<county>, /server-sent-events/district/<page>/<number>; named events are statewidegovernor, countygovernor, statewideussenate, countyussenate, statewideushouse, countyushouse, statewidetnsenate, countytnsenate, statewidetnhouse, countytnhouse, statewideconstitutionalamendment, countyconstitutionalamendment, and 'lastUpdatedTimestamp'; each race event's data is a JSON array of candidates with a chartName. Unverified against a live stream.

election_id: none: the site shows one election at a time ('November 3, 2026 Election' in <h1 id="electionTitle">) and the URLs carry no election id.
discovery: None needed and none available: the same four /categories/<group>/offices URLs serve whatever election is current; check h1#electionTitle for the date. A search result showed the same application at https://www.tnelectionresults.com/home titled 'August 6th, 2026 Unofficial Election Results' (it also 403s the relay UA; not explored), so earlier elections may live on a second host.
cors: The request Origin is reflected: 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://openslate.us' with 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true' (on the HTML pages and the SSE endpoint, when sent with a browser User-Agent). So a browser on openslate.us could read these pages directly.
bot_blocking: Relay User-Agent: 403 from CloudFront ('ERROR: The request could not be satisfied', X-Cache: Error from cloudfront) on https://www.elections.tn.gov/, https://sos.tn.gov/elections/results, https://www.tnelectionresults.com/home and the SSE endpoint. The same requests with a desktop Chrome User-Agent string (plain curl, no cookies, no JavaScript) get 200. So it is a User-Agent filter, not a challenge; the page also loads a Dynatrace RUM script (ruxitagentjs) that is not required.
updated_field: Only through the SSE event 'lastUpdatedTimestamp', which the page writes into <div id="lastUpdatedTimestamp"> as 'Last Updated: <text>'. In the static HTML that div is empty, and the stream was empty when fetched, so I have no example value or zone. (The site ships /js/userTimezone.js, which suggests it converts to the viewer's zone; not read.)

choice_format: JSON inside the data-candidates attribute, entity-encoded in the HTML: [{"name":"Marsha Blackburn","party":"Republican","votes":957136}, …] i.e. {"name":"Marsha Blackburn","party":"Republican","votes":957136}. Party is the full word ('Republican', 'Democratic', 'Independent'). Measures: {"name":"Yes","party":"","votes":1330845} and {"name":"No",…}. The rendered page shows them as 'Marsha Blackburn (R) - 957,136 ✔ 45.52%'.
district_field: Only in the title. Two spellings of it: the data-race attribute and element ids use underscores ('United_States_House_of_Representatives_District_1', id 'chart-United_States_House_of_Representatives_District_1'); the visible <h3 class="chart-title"> and the county-breakdown link use spaces ('/county-breakdown/United%20States%20Senate').
terms: The footer links 'Web and Social Media Policies' at https://sos.tn.gov/web-and-social-media-policies; I could not read it with the relay User-Agent (sos.tn.gov answers 403) and did not fetch it with a browser User-Agent, so no quote. Note the site actively refuses non-browser User-Agents, which is itself a signal about automated access.
